skill.name: near-kit
skill.description: TypeScript library for NEAR Protocol blockchain interaction. Use this skill when writing code that interacts with NEAR Protocol, including viewing contract data, calling contract methods, sending NEAR tokens, building transactions, creating type-safe contract wrappers, integrating wallets (Wallet Selector, HOT Connect), React hooks and providers (@near-kit/react), managing keys, testing with sandbox, meta-transactions (NEP-366), and message signing (NEP-413).
skill.summary: Use near-kit to build NEAR Protocol apps, wallets, transactions, tests, and React integrations with TypeScript.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for near-kit and I found no prompt injection or malware intent. Most static hits are false positives from Markdown fences, TypeScript template strings, placeholder URLs, and local example APIs. Key handling examples and ~/.near-credentials access are real sensitive-use risks that need stronger warnings.

remediation.issue: Direct private key and seed phrase examples
remediation.suggestion: Add clear warnings to never paste real secrets into prompts, logs, or source files. Prefer wallet adapters, secret managers, or restricted function-call keys.
Document permissions, testnet-only examples, backup risks, and safer alternatives such as OS keyrings or explicit user-selected paths.

remediation.issue: Browser and React examples near private key configuration
remediation.suggestion: State that browser code should use wallet adapters only. Keep private keys in trusted server processes or managed key stores.

remediation.issue: Login and relayer examples post signed payloads to APIs
remediation.suggestion: Require nonce expiration, recipient matching, payload validation, and replay protection in all NEP-413 and NEP-366 server examples.

content.value_statement: NEAR integrations often need transaction, wallet, key, and testing patterns. This skill gives concise near-kit examples for TypeScript apps, React hooks, wallets, and sandbox tests.
actual_capabilities: Shows read-only and signed Near client setup for testnet and mainnet.
Explains contract view calls, change calls, token transfers, and transaction builder actions.
Documents Wallet Selector, HOT Connect, and universal server or browser wallet patterns.
Provides React provider, hook, React Query, SWR, and SSR integration patterns.
Covers key stores, seed phrase utilities, sandbox testing, NEP-366, and NEP-413 signing.
limitations: Does not provide the near-kit package source code or implementation internals.
Uses placeholders for keys, accounts, contracts, and endpoints that users must replace safely.
Does not audit smart contract logic or guarantee transaction safety.
Requires users to verify current NEAR network, wallet, and dependency behavior.

use_cases.title: Create a dApp Wallet Flow
use_cases.description: Use React hooks and wallet adapters to connect accounts, call contracts, and display balances.

use_cases.title: Build Server-Side NEAR Automation
use_cases.description: Configure signed transactions, key stores, relayer flows, and message verification for trusted server processes.

use_cases.title: Test Contract Integrations
use_cases.description: Use sandbox examples to create accounts, deploy WASM contracts, call methods, and validate integration behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Read-Only Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to use near-kit to read a NEAR contract view method on testnet. Include imports, client setup, and error handling notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Wallet Calls in React
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add @near-kit/react to a React app. Use wallet-based signing and show the provider, account state, and a contract call.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Transaction Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a near-kit transaction that creates an account, funds it, deploys a contract, and initializes it. Include gas and deposit guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review Keys and Relayers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my near-kit key management and relayer design. Check private key handling, nonce validation, recipient checks, and server-only boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a wallet-connected guestbook call in React.
output: A component-level integration plan using NearProvider, wallet connection state, and a signed contract call.
Notes on signer identity, gas settings, pending states, and user-visible errors.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy and test a NEAR contract locally.
output: A sandbox testing sequence with account creation, contract deployment, initialization, and assertions.
Guidance on unique account names, startup timeouts, and cleanup after tests.

output_examples.input: I need a secure NEP-413 login flow.
output: A client and server flow for message signing, challenge creation, signature verification, and nonce expiration.
Security checks for recipient matching, replay prevention, and trusted backend storage.

best_practices: Use wallet adapters in browsers and keep private keys in trusted server environments only.
Replace example accounts, URLs, gas, and deposit values with values reviewed for the target network.
Add explicit nonce, recipient, expiry, and signer checks for login and meta-transaction flows.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real private keys or seed phrases into prompts, examples, logs, or source files.
Do not use placeholder domains, contract IDs, or account IDs in production deployments.
Do not let browser code manage server private keys or relayer signing keys.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build NEAR Protocol integrations with near-kit, including clients, contracts, wallets, transactions, tests, and React bindings.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I use it for browser wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Wallet Selector and HOT Connect patterns for browser-based signing.

faq.question: Can I use it for backend signing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes server-side examples, but production keys need secret storage and strict access controls.

faq.question: Does it replace NEAR documentation?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused near-kit examples and should be checked against current NEAR and wallet documentation.

faq.question: What security care is required?
faq.answer: Treat private keys, seed phrases, keystore files, signed payloads, and relayer endpoints as sensitive assets.
